slides.heading: Branch Sums
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Branch Sums, an easy binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: List the root-to-leaf path sums, ordered left to right.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. List the root-to-leaf path sums, ordered left to right.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Carry the running sum down each path; at a leaf, that sum is one branch sum.
slides.narration: Carry the running sum down each path; at a leaf, that sum is one branch sum.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Naive: collect each root-to-leaf path, then sum it → O(n·h)
Optimal: carry the running sum down → O(n)
slides.narration: A naive approach stores each full path and sums it at the leaf, repeating work for shared prefixes. Instead we pass the running sum down the recursion, so each node is added exactly once.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Depth-first from the root with sum zero
3. At a leaf, record the sum
4. Recurse left then right to keep left-to-right order
slides.narration: Step by step. First, depth-first from the root with sum zero. Second, add the node's value. Third, at a leaf, record the sum. Fourth, recurse left then right to keep left-to-right order.

slides.caption: Leaf 8: branch sum 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15
slides.narration: Reaching leaf 8, the running total along this path is 15, so we record it.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: The helper takes a node, the running sum and the result list. It adds the node's value, records the sum at a leaf, and otherwise recurses left then right.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: A node is a leaf only if BOTH children are null
slides.narration: The common bug is treating a node with one child as a leaf. A node is a leaf only when both children are null.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Iterative version with an explicit stack
slides.narration: Follow-ups include returning the paths, or checking whether any path sums to a target. You can also do it iteratively with a stack of node and sum pairs.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Carry the running sum down each path; at a leaf, that sum is one branch sum.
slides.narration: To recap Branch Sums: Carry the running sum down each path; at a leaf, that sum is one branch sum. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
